description: Documenting historic buildings damaged by the Nashville tornadoes in March 2020 is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Rebecca Napolitano, Penn State University (psu.edu). The 2020 Nashville Tornado outbreak featured a long-track EF3 tornado that carved a 60-mile path through Nashville, reaching the highest windspeed of 165 mph in Cookeville. It struck downtown Nashville, presenting an opportunity to study the structural vulnerability of older, unreinforced masonry buildings in the downtown area. Coverage: Nashville, TN. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Tornado, Historic buildings, Damage, Reconnaissance. Published 2025-11-18. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
